tricks.original_title: Use Complexity and Intensity, then the kit-piece controls
tricks.reason: The rewrite's central claim, that the Complexity and Intensity sliders belong only to Bass Player and Keyboard Player and 'not the Drummer's', is contradicted. Apple's current 'Edit a Session Player performance' page says settings reached through the Main and Details buttons are common to all Session Players (Bass Player, Keyboard Player and Drummer), and those settings include the Complexity and Intensity sliders. The rewrite keeps only what Apple's Session Player page states.
tricks.final_title: Use Complexity and Intensity, then the kit-piece sliders
tricks.final_body: In the Session Player Editor, drag the Complexity slider up for a busier part and the Intensity slider up for a louder one. Apple lists both as settings common to all Session Players, Drummer included. Then click Details and drag the kit piece sliders to set the complexity range of individual kit pieces.

sources.label: Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac
sources.evidence: Says many Session Player Editor settings, reached with the Main and Details buttons, are common to all Session Players (Bass Player, Keyboard Player and Drummer). You drag the Complexity or Intensity slider, and higher settings give more complexity or intensity (loudness). tricks.original_title: Change the drummer, not just the preset
tricks.reason: The lock advice is right, but the text presented as Apple's words was misquoted. Apple says the lock prevents 'any changes to the fills setting', not 'the setting'. tricks.final_title: Change the drummer, not just the preset
tricks.final_body: Each drummer has its own kit and playing style, so if a preset is close but the feel is wrong, try another drummer. Lock the fills first if you like them: Apple says the lock stops 'any changes to the fills setting when switching presets or drummers.'

tricks.original_title: Turn individual kit pieces on and off per region
tricks.reason: Apple's current Drummer page says you mute and unmute kit and percussion pieces by clicking them. It also says changes in the editor affect only the selected region, not the whole track.
tricks.final_title: Turn individual kit pieces on and off per region
tricks.final_body: Click a kit piece in the editor to enable or disable it for that region only. Drop the crash out of the verse and back in for the chorus.

sources.evidence: You can mute and unmute drum kit and percussion pieces by clicking them. Any changes or selections you make in the Drummer Editor affect only the selected region, not the entire track.

tricks.original_title: Convert a Drummer region to MIDI and edit it by hand
tricks.reason: Apple's current page gives the path: Control-click (right-click) the region, then choose Convert > Convert to MIDI Region. It says the result behaves like any other MIDI region and can be edited in the Piano Roll Editor.
tricks.final_title: Convert a Drummer region to MIDI and edit it by hand
tricks.final_body: Right‑click the region and choose Convert > Convert to MIDI Region. You get the full performance in the Piano Roll to nudge, delete and re‑velocity as you like.

tricks.original_title: Use the Details panel for feel, ghost notes and hi‑hat
tricks.reason: Apple's Drummer page says clicking the Details button shows the Feel knob (right plays ahead of the beat, left plays behind it), Ghost Notes (syncopated snare and kick hits), the Hi-Hat knob (how open or closed) and the Humanize knob. All four controls and the Details button name are confirmed.
tricks.final_title: Use the Details panel for feel, ghost notes and hi‑hat
tricks.final_body: Click the Details button in the Drummer Editor to reveal Feel (drag right to play ahead of the beat, left to play behind it), Ghost Notes (syncopated snare and kick hits), Hi-Hat openness and Humanize. This is where a stiff pattern becomes a groove.

sources.label: Apple — Edit a Drummer performance in Logic Pro for Mac
sources.evidence: Clicking the Details button shows the Humanize knob (patterns that are not perfectly quantized), the Feel knob (right = ahead of the beat, left = behind), the Ghost Notes knob (syncopated snare and kick hits) and the Hi-Hat knob (how far the hi-hat opens and closes).

tricks.original_title: Swap the kit without losing the performance
tricks.reason: Most of the text checks out: the Drum Kit Designer / Drum Machine Designer split, Tune, Dampen and Gain per piece, and the Overheads and Room switches on multi-channel kits. tricks.final_title: Swap and tune kit pieces in Drum Kit Designer
tricks.final_body: Acoustic drummers use Drum Kit Designer; electronic drummers use Drum Machine Designer. In Drum Kit Designer, click a kit piece to open its Edit and Exchange panes. Swap the kick or snare (toms, cymbals and hi-hat too on multi-channel kits) and set Tune, Dampen (sustain) and Gain per piece. Multi-channel kits add Overheads and Room (A, B or off) switches.

sources.label: Apple — Drum Kit Designer Edit pane in Logic Pro for Mac
sources.evidence: The Tune knob sets the selected piece's pitch, Dampen its sustain and Gain its volume. The Overheads switch (multi-channel kits only) includes the overhead mic. The Room switch (multi-channel kits only) chooses room A or B or turns room emulation off.

sources.label: Apple — Use Drum Kit Designer in Logic Pro for Mac
sources.evidence: Clicking a kit piece opens the Edit pane and Exchange pane. On all kits you can exchange kick and snare; on multi-channel kits also toms, cymbals and hi-hat.

tricks.final_title: Drag any audio file straight onto a pad
tricks.final_body: Drag a WAV, AIFF or MP3 from the Finder, a Logic Pro browser, or a region from the Tracks area onto a pad. Drum Machine Designer inserts a new Quick Sampler instance on a new subtrack for that pad automatically.

tricks.reason: Apple says each pad subtrack has its own channel strip that you can process on its own in the mixer. The Mixer key X is documented as View > Show Mixer (or press X).
tricks.final_title: Every pad is its own channel strip

tricks.final_title: Copy a pad with Control-click
tricks.final_body: To copy a pad, Control-click it and choose Copy. Then Control-click the pad you want to replace and choose Paste. Cut works the same way. Dragging a pad to an empty location in the grid reorders it rather than copying it.

sources.label: Apple — Use Drum Machine Designer pad controls in Logic Pro for Mac

tricks.final_title: Use Pad Controls for quick shaping
tricks.final_body: Select a pad and click Pad Controls in the bar below the grid. The pad's tone and effect parameters appear in the Plug-in pane. For Quick Sampler pads, Q-Sampler Main shows the waveform editor and Q-Sampler Details shows the LFOs and the pitch, filter and amp envelopes. Drum Synth pads get a Drum Synth button.

sources.label: Apple — Use Drum Machine Designer pad controls in Logic Pro for Mac

tricks.original_title: Use the main stack fader for the whole kit
tricks.reason: Apple supports the claim that DMD is a track stack and that plug-ins on a summing stack's main track affect all subtracks. The text was reworded to Apple's terms (main track, audio subgroup). Apple's caveat about subtracks routed outside the stack was added.
tricks.final_title: Use the main track for the whole kit
tricks.final_body: A Drum Machine Designer kit is a track stack. Plug-ins on its main track affect every subtrack, so put your kit compressor and limiter there. Any pad whose output you route outside the stack skips that processing.

sources.label: Apple — Logic Pro for Mac track stacks overview

If you route subtracks to a destination outside the stack, they are no longer affected by the controls on the main track.

tricks.final_title: Save your kit as a patch
tricks.final_body: In Drum Machine Designer, select the kit name pad at the top, then click Save at the bottom of the Library. The patch holds the main track and every subtrack with its channel strip and plug-in settings. If only a single pad is selected, you save just that kit piece.
